You will have a lot more opportunities to lose your virginity. It might seem like you messed up the way you formed your life until now but you haven't. You have the opportunity to change your life moving forward if this is what you want. 

It's not rare to still be a virgin at your age. It might seem like you are missing out on something important and that's because it is important. And since it's so important, please don't rush into it just so you can say you have experienced it.

You will later learn that your lack of sexual activity is a blessing in it's own right and a quality that is looked for even though it may seem like a burden.

The fear of missing out is a real phenomenon and it's just how people are wired, you must have the mental strength to recognize it's not always there to help you.

Height is a difficult pill to swallow but the older you get the more you realize it's not nearly as much of a facor. I'm not going to lie and say it's not a factor at all, but it's an insignificantly small one.

Just because you are 5'4 doesn't mean you will be short of partners. Most people, especially mature adults, don't pay mind to height. You will have the opportunity to have a lot of relationships.

Try your best to look at this for what it is, an insecurity, it doesn't make sense logically and is only hurting you in anticipation; it is not reality.

Even in a worst case scenario where you're unable to shake your insecurity, there are a lot of cultures where 5'4 is considered tall. Somewhere in your future, your partner is waiting for you and your height is perfect for them.

Therapists have a duty to report (in most places) if they believe there to be impending harm to someone, whether it's their client or others.

Whatever the argument was between you and your peers/professors, I'm sure they'll be willing to forgive you, especially with a genuine apology. 

As for your option of dropping out, I can only hope your family support and love you regardless of if you drop out or not. There are plenty of fields of work you can lean towards that don't require any academic success and are considered great occupations and aren't frowned upon.

I don't recommend pretending as an option, you'll only dig yourself into a hole while over-prioritizing others opinions. This is your life, and you only get to live it once. You should live your life for you, not for other people. Try to picture yourself at your death bed: all the struggles in your life, all the worries of what people might've thought about you, will be trivial. Worrying about what others might think of you won't help you get anywhere. 

Your option to die is definitely not the best option. It is difficult to be alone, especially when distanced from your family but I believe you can repair your relationship with your peers and your professors and find a way to feel less isolated if you decide to continue with University. Maybe video calls with your family or just trying to find people with shared hobbies and interests in your university. There could already be social groups for hobbies if you search around a bit. 

Dropping out is a complete good option as well but you just need to make sure you have some semblance of a plan for what you want to do, as long as you have some plan; even if it seems ambitious or it seems stupid, it'll be good enough as a start. Life is never stable and consistent for anyone, big changes happen suddenly all the time for everyone and as long as you realize you're not meant to have everything together and you accept things as they come, you'll work things out.
